subject: AI Squared dedicated-pool saturation — evidence request & next steps
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@aisquared.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: support@aisquared.com
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool saturation observed — intermittent 503s during peak window

Jonas,

We saw recurring 503s and timeouts from our dedicated pool this morning during our morning batch scoring run (08:45-09:30 PT). Error rate spiked to ~12% for ~18 minutes and our fallback to hosted models returned degraded latency. We captured scheduler logs and a screenshot of the queue metrics.

Can you confirm whether this was a capacity saturation or autoscaler lag on your side? Our SREs want any logs you can share and an ETA for a fix — this is affecting our fraud-detection pipeline during a high-traffic window.

Attached: scheduler-logs-20290503.txt (excerpt), pool-metrics-20290503.png (screenshot)

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Head of Platform Engineering
AI Squared
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@aisquared.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool saturation observed — intermittent 503s during peak window

Laura — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. We see the same spike on our telemetry for your reserved pool (pool_id: rsvd-aisq-01). Initial read: a short-lived surge in concurrent active contexts combined with delayed node warmups in the autoscaler.

Immediate steps we're taking:
- Marissa is kicking off deeper traces and pulling control-plane logs for the window you provided.
- We’ll correlate your scheduler logs with our allocator timeline to identify hot tenants and contention.
- Ben will coordinate a brief follow-up to discuss short-term mitigation (burst capacity / manual node add).

We’ll send a targeted data package to you within 3 hours. If you can share the exact job IDs that were running at 08:45-09:30, that will speed correlation.

Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@aisquared.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool saturation observed — initial findings and evidence request

Laura / Jonas — I pulled the allocator and autoscaler traces for rsvd-aisq-01. What we see in the 08:40-09:10 window:

- Autoscaler requested 4 additional nodes at 08:41:14 but node warmup times (NVLink init + model load) were ~5x longer than baseline due to concurrent large-model warmups from two other tenants sharing the same hardware class.
- Our KV cache eviction rate increased, which contributed to earlier token recomputation for in-flight requests.
- Tail latencies for the tenant queue crossed our 95th pct SLAs intermittently, resulting in 503s when the per-tenant queue reached configured max inflight.

For a complete postmortem and to validate mitigations, can you provide:
- The job IDs / run IDs for the scoring jobs that were active 08:45-09:30 (helps map request IDs to your traces)
- Any custom model-serve settings (long-context pinned models, forced quantization) used by your jobs

We’re assembling an evidence bundle (logs, allocator timeline, scheduler crosswalk) and plan to share an export in about 3 hours. We’ll also propose a short-term capacity bump for your reserved pool to cover peak windows while we tune warmup concurrency.

Attachment: excerpt from allocator timeline (included in export)

—Marissa
Senior Customer Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@aisquared.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool saturation observed — temporary mitigation and credit offer

Hi Laura — thanks for working through this with us. Based on the traces Marissa pulled, we can offer the following immediate options to reduce customer impact while we root-cause and prepare a postmortem:

1) Short-term reserved burst: schedule 2 warm standby nodes in your pool for the next 7 days (manual add) — estimated cost delta: $1,200/day.
2) Autoscaler tune: reduce max concurrent model-warmups from 4 -> 2 for rsvd-aisq-01 during your high window (we’ll monitor impact).
3) Credit: We will offer a one-time service credit of 15% on your May invoice for the affected window, conditional on acceptance by 2029-05-10.

If you’d like us to immediately enable option (1) we can do it now and rollback after a week. Otherwise we’ll enable (2) tonight at 23:00 PT and watch the morning window tomorrow.

Also attaching a short export that contains the scheduler-allocator crosswalk and raw 503 request IDs for your SRE correlation.

Attachments: scheduler-allocator-crosswalk-ARS-8347.csv

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@aisquared.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 4 May 2029 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool saturation observed — next steps, timeline, and postmortem deliverable

Laura — following up with a consolidated plan and timeline. Thank you for sharing the job IDs; we used them to validate a correlated trace. Summary and next steps:

Summary: A short spike in concurrent model warmups across capacity-shared nodes caused delayed node readiness; the autoscaler issued scale actions but warmup latency allowed the tenant queue to hit max inflight briefly, triggering 503s. KV eviction contributed to elevated compute for in-flight requests.

Action items and timeline:
- 2029-05-04 18:00 PT: We enabled autoscaler conservative mode (max concurrent warmups = 2) for rsvd-aisq-01 (temporary).
- 2029-05-05 08:00 PT: If you agree, we will provision 2 warm standby nodes for one week (manual burst) to cover peak hours; ops will monitor and report metrics daily.
- 2029-05-07 12:00 PT: Draft postmortem shared (includes logs, timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations).
- 2029-05-09 15:00 PT: Live review with AI Squared SREs to go over the postmortem and validate long-term mitigations.

We will include the evidence bundle (allocator timeline, host-level logs, your scheduler excerpts) in the postmortem. We’ll also propose a long-term change: tenant-aware warmup isolation to prevent large-model warmups from blocking others on the same hardware class.

Please confirm whether you accept the 1-week warm standby proposal and the credit offer (Ben’s 15% on May invoice). If you prefer not to take the paid standby, we’ll keep the autoscaler tuning and accelerate the longer-term isolation work.

Attachment: postincident-draft-20290504.pdf (draft postmortem, internal + customer sections)

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
